description: Quantify signal robustness via moving block bootstrap on Sharpe ratio and permutation testing on signal IC, then compare resampling-based to naive parametric confidence intervals.
agent_prompt: Quantify the robustness of a momentum signal on /workspace/data/BTCUSDT_1d_2021_2024.csv via resampling methods. Define the signal as 20-day price momentum: signal[t] = (close[t] - close[t-20]) / close[t-20]. Strategy: position[t+1] = sign(signal[t]) (long/short, no costs unless you choose to add). Compute strategy daily returns. Then: (1) Moving block bootstrap CI on Sharpe ratio — block_size=20, n_resamples=1000. Write /workspace/output/bootstrap_results.json with sharpe_observed, sharpe_mean_resampled, sharpe_ci_95_low, sharpe_ci_95_high, n_resamples, block_size. (2) Permutation test on IC — under H0 that signal is independent of forward 1d return, randomly permute the forward-return series 1000 times and recompute Spearman IC each time. Write /workspace/output/permutation_test.json with observed_ic, p_value, ic_mean_under_null, ic_std_under_null, n_permutations. (3) Compute a naive parametric 95% CI for Sharpe assuming i.i.d. normal returns: Sharpe_observed +/- 1.96 * sqrt((1 + 0.5*Sharpe_observed**2)/n_obs). Write /workspace/output/comparison.md tabling bootstrap CI vs parametric CI side by side and explaining which is wider and why (autocorrelation in returns inflates the true sampling variance beyond the iid assumption).

required_capabilities: Implement moving block bootstrap on time series returns
Compute bootstrap CIs for Sharpe ratio with explicit block size
Run permutation test for signal-return independence
Compute naive parametric Sharpe CI using the iid normal approximation
Compare resampling-based vs parametric CI and explain the difference
